[untitled BTM module] No single physiological programme unites these genes; the group is best read as a loose collection spanning lipid storage, growth-factor feedback, small RNA transcription and nutrient transport, several of whose members remain uncharacterised open reading frames or polymerase-related pseudogene sequences. The better-defined components point to distinct processes: a perilipin-family protein coats lipid droplets and governs regulated triglyceride mobilisation in oxidative tissues such as heart and muscle; a TGF-β- and androgen-inducible membrane protein acts in negative feedback on that signalling and is frequently overexpressed in prostate cancer; a Ras-association domain protein of the tumour-suppressor family couples Ras signalling to apoptosis; a sodium-coupled transporter carries short-chain fatty acids and lactate across the intestinal and renal epithelium; and a subunit of the snRNA-activating protein complex drives transcription of the spliceosomal snRNA genes.

[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the myeloid identity and activation program of monocytes and macrophages, the cells that patrol tissue for microbes and debris and set the tone of an inflammatory response. The transcription factor SPI1 (PU.1) specifies this lineage together with HHEX, while TLR4 senses bacterial lipopolysaccharide and PTAFR responds to platelet-activating factor, coupling through the Src-family kinase LYN, the phospholipase PLCB2 and the ITAM-bearing adaptor TYROBP (DAP12) to calcium mobilization and cytoskeletal change; DOK2 acts as a brake on this kinase signaling.
